history.note: First versioned benchmark. Oasis by the Sea construction (and the diagnostic benchmarks) at 25 game minutes on a fixed game speed of 40, minimum turn 8 game seconds, default wait 5, context budget 120,000; reading-only replies cost game time from the 12th in a row; 4 replies without a tool call end the run; growth measured from the do-nothing baseline; resumable series with infrastructure failures run again.
The uncommitted-change check (harness.dirty) covers only the fingerprinted files; play and scoring are unchanged.
Clearer stop reason in the series record and runner log; play and scoring are unchanged.
Broken provider streams (OpenRouter's "JSON error injected into SSE stream") and plain 429 rate limits are retried like other transient errors; what the model sees and the scoring are unchanged.
Version numbers follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); v1 is renamed 1.0.0. No change in behaviour.
Claude through Anthropic's own Messages API: adaptive thinking at the profile's effort, cache marks for that API

Stockpile and granary storage (piles, room per good, full notes) in observations and status; the stockpile pile rule in the prompt; place_near and expand_storage anchor by building type, so stockpiles expand on every side; market_trade says whether gold or storage stopped a purchase; a raw building-record diagnostic in the probe; the prompt says only quarries use oxen, several ox tethers can serve one quarry and stone piling up at a quarry means more are needed
The package version (package.json, package-lock.json) is the benchmark version, and bump sets it; no change in behaviour.
Buildings with workers keep one open side: spot finding, retries and a check of build_structure targets; tile map read in the background while paused
Each finished episode is saved in the game and copied into the run folder; no change in what a run plays or scores

Runs record their cost on every endpoint: model profiles off OpenRouter have prices, applied to each request's tokens, a run cannot start without them, and npm run cost prices earlier runs. Play and scoring unchanged.

The reader forces a garbage collection when the game's collector stalls (no collection for 20 s while the managed heap grew 64 MiB) and records the collector's state; memory samples carry the managed heap and forced collections are logged as gc_watchdog events. The task, prompts, tools and scoring are unchanged.
Adds npm run episodes -- --human, a reference game played by a person: loaded, paused when the game-time budget is used up, scored, screenshotted and saved. Agent runs play and score the same.

The agent is told population and popularity count beside net worth (weighting not given); episodes are independent unless --playbook; status shows worker efficiency, the food factor once and religion with the church bonus; the reader reads the church bonus and the keep's tax figure, which set_tax returns; new set_rations tool; build_structure places good and bad things.

Agent runs play and are scored the same. After each episode that counts, npm run episodes interviews the agent in its own conversation with the tools off (--no-interview leaves it out): its result beside the reference game a person played on its map, then four questions. Every run the runner makes (episodes, reference games, do-nothing baselines, dry runs) records the whole state at its end in results.json and results.md; the reader counts the player's buildings by type for them, which the agent is not shown. Records the reference games on Oasis by the Sea and Large Barren Desert and the do-nothing baselines of both benchmark start saves at 33 1/3 game minutes.

Status and each observation's stats count the church and cathedral bonus in points: the reader gives it in the factors' units (25 per point), so 1.2.0 showed a church and a cathedral as religion +75 instead of +3. The task, prompts, tool definitions and scoring are unchanged.

Compaction no longer triggers early from a stale byte-based estimate; build_structure's exit click targets the last attempted placement and the construction tray's open category is remembered across calls; input-only tool clicks reuse a short-lived frame cache instead of recapturing the screen; removed the unused list_buildings, guide_page and notebook_edit tools; build_structure also takes map-tile targets (tile_x/tile_y, projected from the live camera, with a not_on_screen status) and find_sites works without a screenshot; wait_and_observe can skip its screenshot (screenshot: false), and the new run setting fallbackObservation (default when-needed) makes the host's fallback after a turn without game_action, inspect_building or a pixel placement a text-only observation; the construction guide is sent as a JPEG when installed; screenshots stay in the conversation until compaction so every request repeats the previous one for the prompt cache; failed or partial tool results carry a remedy naming the tool call that addresses them; the episode runner recognises the main menu and Load Game dialog instead of waiting out fixed timeouts; the prompt no longer places the granary near the keep and says the ground close to the keep is critical for buildings whose efficiency matters more there; find_sites groups its spots by the ground under them, and spots the harness picks itself keep off other buildings' ground (oasis grass, stone, iron ore, oil); new tool demolish_building removes one of the agent's buildings, given by tile or pixel; the model's screenshots are scaled down to 1280 x 720 by default (run setting screenshotWidth), and the runner clicks through the startup screens; acting tools spend less game time on their own steps (the clicks they send are unchanged): go_to_tile and navigate_minimap click the minimap with the game still paused when nothing in the reply has unpaused it yet, place_near and expand_storage read the tile map while selecting the building, and tools that send input without looking at the screen reuse the latest capture while it is under 20 s old; a good's room in storage counts the empty piles, and an empty granary adds 250 to the granary room.

The preparation request carries the gameplay tools, so the first gameplay request reads it from the provider's prompt cache, and a preparation reply that calls a tool is asked again; observation stats list only the goods in stock and the prompt says an unlisted good has none; tool parameters that take one of a list of names are plain JSON Schema enums instead of unions of literals, about a quarter fewer bytes in the tool list every request repeats.

market_trade trades in the game's own steps (a purchase 5 units a click; a sale 20 while 100 or more are in stock, 10 from 50, else 5) up to lots x 5 units and never more, counting a click only when the reader shows that trade; its description no longer says food trades in lots of 10.
The max reasoning level (Claude's max effort, OpenRouter's xhigh) is a model setting; runs record it, and what a run plays and scores is unchanged.
Moonshot profiles send Kimi K3's reasoning levels (low, high, max) as reasoning_effort
Add the Large Barren Desert construction scenario; Oasis runs see nothing new
Large Barren Desert rules give the whole starting package and say part of it waits for storage room
The finished game's save clears the whole name field; what a run plays is unchanged
Waiting reminder after 3 game minutes without an economy action; trees told from cacti; the desert rules lose their tree sentence
